title: East of the Sun and West of the Moon

chapterList.title: A Poor Family
also: The White Bear at the Door

s.t: A poor family lived in a small house.
s.fr: Une famille pauvre vivait dans une petite maison.

s.t: The father and mother had little money and little food.
s.fr: Le père et la mère avaient peu d’argent et peu de nourriture.

s.t: They had three daughters, and the youngest was the kindest.
s.fr: Ils avaient trois filles, et la plus jeune était la plus gentille.

s.t: She helped her mother with the work every day.
s.fr: Elle aidait sa mère avec le travail chaque jour.

paras.summary: A poor family of five lives in a small house with little money, and of the three daughters, the youngest is the kindest and helps her mother with the work every day.

s.t: Soon, the little food they had was almost gone.
s.fr: Bientôt, le peu de nourriture qu’ils avaient était presque épuisé.

s.t: "We have so little food," the mother said one night.
s.fr: « Nous avons si peu de nourriture, » dit la mère un soir.

s.t: "We will manage," the father said.
s.fr: « Nous nous en sortirons, » dit le père.

s.t: The youngest daughter said little, but she was afraid.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille dit peu, mais elle avait peur.

s.t: She wished to help her poor family.
s.fr: Elle souhaitait aider sa pauvre famille.

paras.summary: One winter the family's food is almost gone, and though the mother and father worry aloud, the youngest daughter stays quiet, only wishing she could help.

s.t: That night, a storm came to the house.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, une tempête arriva à la maison.

s.t: Wind beat against the small house.
s.fr: Le vent frappa contre la petite maison.

s.t: Snow fell, and the wind was cold.
s.fr: La neige tomba, et le vent était froid.

s.t: The three daughters sat by the fire.
s.fr: Les trois filles étaient assises près du feu.

s.t: Someone knocked at the door.
s.fr: Quelqu’un frappa à la porte.

s.t: The knock came again.
s.fr: Le coup vint de nouveau.

s.t: The father stood and walked to the door.
s.fr: Le père se leva et marcha vers la porte.

paras.summary: A storm comes that night, wind beating against the house as snow falls and the cold deepens, and the father is afraid of the storm; as the three daughters sit by the fire, a knock sounds at the door, then again, so the father goes to answer it.

s.t: The father opened the door.
s.fr: Le père ouvrit la porte.

s.t: A white bear stood in the storm.
s.fr: Un ours blanc se tenait dans la tempête.

s.t: The father stepped back.
s.fr: Le père recula.

s.t: "Do not be afraid," the white bear said.
s.fr: « N’ayez pas peur, » dit-il, l’ours blanc.

s.t: "I will make your family rich," the bear said.
s.fr: « Je rendrai votre famille riche, » dit-il, l’ours.

paras.summary: The father opens the door to find a white bear in the storm, and though he steps back afraid, the bear tells him not to fear and promises to make his family rich.

s.t: "Give me your youngest daughter," the bear said.
s.fr: « Donnez-moi votre fille la plus jeune, » dit-il le ours.

s.t: The father did not want to lose his daughter.
s.fr: Le père ne voulait pas perdre sa fille.

s.t: The father called the mother and the three daughters to the door.
s.fr: Le père appela la mère et les trois filles à la porte.

s.t: He told them what the white bear wanted.
s.fr: Il leur dit ce que l’ours blanc voulait.

paras.summary: The bear asks for the youngest daughter in return, and though the father does not want to lose her, the family has little money and little food, so he calls the mother and the three daughters to the door and tells them what the bear wants.

s.t: "Where would she live?" the mother asked the bear.
s.fr: « Où vivrait-elle ? » demanda la mère à l’ours.

s.t: "In a castle, far from here," said the bear.
s.fr: « Dans un château, loin d’ici, » dit l’ours.

s.t: "She will have all she needs there," the bear said.
s.fr: « Elle aura là tout ce dont elle a besoin, » dit l’ours.

s.t: The three daughters looked at the white bear.
s.fr: Les trois filles regardèrent l’ours blanc.

s.t: "What do you say?" the bear asked the youngest daughter.
s.fr: « Que dites-vous ? » demanda l’ours à la fille la plus jeune.

paras.summary: The mother, afraid for her daughter, asks where she would live, and the bear answers: a castle far away, where she would have all she needs; then the bear turns to the youngest daughter and asks what she says.

s.t: The youngest daughter looked at her mother and father.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune regarda sa mère et son père.

s.t: She thought of the little money and the little food.
s.fr: Elle pensa à le peu d’argent et à le peu de nourriture.

s.t: If she went with the bear, her family would be rich.
s.fr: Si elle partait avec l’ours, sa famille serait riche.

s.t: But she did not know the white bear at all.
s.fr: Mais elle ne connaissait pas du tout l’ours blanc.

s.t: She was afraid to leave her home.
s.fr: Elle avait peur de quitter sa maison.

s.t: She decided to go with the bear.
s.fr: Elle décida de partir avec l’ours.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter weighs her family's poverty against her fear of the unknown white bear, and after she thinks and thinks, she decides to go with him.

s.t: "I will go with you," she said to the bear.
s.fr: « Je partirai avec toi, » dit-elle à l’ours.

s.t: Her mother cried.
s.fr: Sa mère pleura.

s.t: The father and mother said goodbye to their daughter.
s.fr: Le père et la mère dirent à le revoir à leur fille.

s.t: The other daughters said goodbye to her too.
s.fr: Les autres filles lui dirent à le revoir aussi.

paras.summary: She tells the bear she will go, and her mother cries as the whole family says goodbye to her.

s.t: The white bear told her to climb onto his back.
s.fr: L’ours blanc lui dit de monter sur son dos.

s.t: She held onto the bear, and he ran into the storm.
s.fr: Elle s’accrocha à l’ours, et il courut dans la tempête.

s.t: He ran through the night.
s.fr: Il courut toute la nuit.

paras.summary: The white bear has her climb onto his back, and holding on, she rides as he runs into the storm and through the night, until her home is far away.

s.t: The bear and the youngest daughter came to a mountain.
s.fr: L’ours et la plus jeune fille arrivèrent à une montagne.

s.t: A castle stood in the mountain.
s.fr: Un château se dressait dans la montagne.

s.t: The castle had rooms of gold.
s.fr: Le château avait des salles d’or.

s.t: The bear gave the youngest daughter a room.
s.fr: L’ours donna une chambre à la plus jeune fille.

s.t: She had never seen so much gold before.
s.fr: Elle n’avait jamais vu autant d’or auparavant.

s.t: But she still missed her family.
s.fr: Mais elle regrettait encore sa famille.

paras.summary: The bear brings the youngest daughter to a castle inside a mountain, full of rooms of gold, and gives her a room of her own, but even with so much gold, she still misses her family and thinks of her mother and father at night.

s.t: One night, she went to bed, and the room grew dark.
s.fr: Une nuit, elle alla se coucher, et la chambre devint sombre.

s.t: Someone came in and lay down beside her.
s.fr: Quelqu’un entra et s’allongea à côté d’elle.

s.t: She did not see his face, and she did not know who he was.
s.fr: Elle ne vit pas son visage, et elle ne sut pas qui il était.

s.t: Before light came, he was gone.
s.fr: Avant que la lumière arrive, il était parti.

paras.summary: One night she goes to bed, the room grows dark, and someone comes in and lies down beside her, but she cannot see his face or know who he is.

s.t: Night after night, someone came to her in the dark.
s.fr: Nuit après nuit, quelqu’un venait la voir dans l’obscurité.

s.t: She wanted to light a candle and look at him.
s.fr: Elle voulait allumer une bougie et le regarder.

s.t: But she was too afraid.
s.fr: Mais elle avait trop peur.

paras.summary: Night after night, someone comes to her in the dark, and sometimes she wants to light a candle and look at him, but she is too afraid to try; she never asks who he is, and though she has food, gold, and a rich home, she does not know the man in the dark.

s.t: One day, the youngest daughter came to the bear.
s.fr: Un jour, la plus jeune fille vint voir l’ours.

s.t: "May I visit my mother and father?" she asked.
s.fr: « Puis-je rendre visite à ma mère et à mon père ? » demanda-t-elle.

s.t: The white bear thought about this.
s.fr: L’ours blanc réfléchit à cela.

s.t: "You may go and see them," the bear said.
s.fr: « Tu peux aller les voir, » dit l’ours.

paras.summary: One day the youngest daughter comes to the bear and asks if she may visit her mother and father, and the bear agrees to let her go and see them.

s.t: "But there is one rule," said the bear.
s.fr: « Mais il y a une règle, » dit l’ours.

s.t: "Never talk with your mother alone," the bear said.
s.fr: « Ne parle jamais avec ta mère seule, » dit l’ours.

s.t: "Why not?" the youngest daughter asked.
s.fr: « Pourquoi pas ? » demanda la plus jeune fille.

s.t: "If you do, trouble will come to us both," said the bear.
s.fr: « Si tu fais cela, des ennuis viendront à nous deux, » dit l’ours.

s.t: She did not know why, but she agreed to the rule.
s.fr: Elle ne savait pas pourquoi, mais elle accepta la règle.

s.t: "I will not talk with my mother alone," she said.
s.fr: « Je ne parlerai pas avec ma mère seule, » dit-elle.

paras.summary: The bear says there is one rule, never to talk with her mother alone, warning that trouble will come to them both if she does, and though she does not know why, she agrees.

s.t: The white bear ran with her back to her home.
s.fr: L’ours blanc courut avec elle jusqu’à sa maison.

s.t: Her mother held her and looked at her rich clothes.
s.fr: Sa mère la tint dans ses bras et regarda ses riches vêtements.

s.t: "You look rich," her mother said.
s.fr: « Tu as l’air riche, » dit sa mère.

s.t: The youngest daughter told her family about the castle and the gold.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille parla à sa famille du château et de l’or.

s.t: But she did not tell them about the man in the dark.
s.fr: Mais elle ne leur parla pas de l’homme dans l’obscurité.

paras.summary: The white bear runs with her back to her home, where her mother and father are glad to see her; her mother holds her hand, looks at her rich clothes, and tells her she looks rich, so she tells her family about the castle and the gold, but not about the man in the dark.

s.t: The mother asked to speak with her daughter alone.
s.fr: La mère demanda à parler seule avec sa fille.

s.t: The youngest daughter thought of the bear's rule.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille pensa à la règle de l’ours.

s.t: "I will not talk with you alone," she said.
s.fr: « Je ne parlerai pas avec vous seule, » dit-elle.

s.t: "Why not?" her mother asked.
s.fr: « Pourquoi pas ? » demanda sa mère.

paras.summary: The mother asks to speak with her daughter alone, but the youngest daughter thinks of the bear's rule and says she will not, and when her mother asks why, she stays still.

s.t: Her mother was afraid for her.
s.fr: Sa mère avait peur pour elle.

s.t: "That man may be a troll," her mother said.
s.fr: « Cet homme est peut-être un troll, » dit sa mère.

s.t: But she was afraid for her mother too.
s.fr: Mais elle avait aussi peur pour sa mère.

s.t: She agreed to talk with her mother alone.
s.fr: Elle accepta de parler seule avec sa mère.

paras.summary: Her mother, afraid for her, says the man may be a troll, and though the youngest daughter thinks of what the bear had said, she is afraid for her mother too, so she agrees to talk with her alone.

s.t: She told her mother about the man in the dark room.
s.fr: Elle parla à sa mère de l’homme dans la chambre sombre.

s.t: "I never see his face," she said.
s.fr: « Je ne vois jamais son visage, » dit-elle.

s.t: Her mother gave her a candle.
s.fr: Sa mère lui donna une bougie.

s.t: "Light this at night, and look at his face," her mother said.
s.fr: « Allume-la la nuit, et regarde son visage, » dit-elle.

s.t: The youngest daughter took the candle.
s.fr: La fille cadette prit la bougie.

s.t: Soon the white bear came to take her back to the castle far away.
s.fr: Bientôt l’ours blanc vint la ramener au château lointain.

s.t: She hid the candle in her clothes.
s.fr: Elle cacha la bougie dans ses vêtements.

paras.summary: She tells her mother about the man in the dark room, who she never sees, so her mother gives her a candle and tells her to light it at night and look at his face; the youngest daughter takes the candle, and when the white bear comes to take her back to the castle, she hides it in her clothes.

chapterList.title: The Candle in the Night
also: East of the Sun and West of the Moon

s.t: That night, someone came to the dark room.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, quelqu’un vint dans la chambre sombre.

s.t: Soon she knew he was asleep.
s.fr: Bientôt elle sut qu’il dormait.

s.t: She took the candle and lit the room.
s.fr: Elle prit la bougie et éclaira la chambre.

s.t: In the light, she saw a young man.
s.fr: Dans la lumière, elle vit un jeune homme.

paras.summary: Back at the castle, she still hides the candle, and that night, when someone comes into the dark room, she soon knows he is asleep, takes out the candle, and lights it.

s.t: She kissed him.
s.fr: Elle l’embrassa.

s.t: Three drops of hot wax fell on his shirt.
s.fr: Trois gouttes de cire chaude tombèrent sur sa chemise.

s.t: The young man woke.
s.fr: Le jeune homme se réveilla.

paras.summary: In the light she sees a handsome young man, and after she looks at his face, she kisses him, but three drops of hot wax fall on his shirt, and he wakes.

s.t: He looked at the candle she held.
s.fr: Il regarda la bougie qu’elle tenait.

s.t: He looked at the wax on his shirt.
s.fr: Il regarda la cire sur sa chemise.

s.t: "What have you done?" he said.
s.fr: « Qu’avez-vous fait ? » dit-il.

s.t: "I wanted to see your face," she said.
s.fr: « Je voulais voir votre visage, » dit-elle.

s.t: The young man looked sad.
s.fr: Le jeune homme avait l’air triste.

s.t: "You should not have done this," he said.
s.fr: « Vous n’auriez pas dû faire cela, » dit-il.

paras.summary: He looks at the candle she held and the wax on his shirt and asks what she has done; the youngest daughter, afraid, says she wanted to see his face, but the young man looks sad and tells her she should not have done this.

s.t: "I am a prince," the young man said.
s.fr: « Je suis un prince, » dit le jeune homme.

s.t: "A troll's curse fell on me," he said.
s.fr: « La malédiction d’un troll tomba sur moi, » dit-il.

s.t: The youngest daughter was afraid.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille avait peur.

paras.summary: The young man says he is a prince, and a troll's curse fell on him, so the youngest daughter is afraid.

s.t: "You have lived here almost one year," he said.
s.fr: « Vous avez vécu ici presque un an, » dit-il.

s.t: "A little more, and the curse would have ended."
s.fr: « Un peu plus, et la malédiction aurait pris fin. »

s.t: "But now you have seen my face."
s.fr: « Mais maintenant vous avez vu mon visage. »

s.t: He looked at the wax on his shirt.
s.fr: Il regarda la cire sur sa chemise.

s.t: The prince looked sad.
s.fr: Le prince avait l’air triste.

s.t: The youngest daughter did not know what to say.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille ne savait pas quoi dire.

paras.summary: He tells her she has lived there almost one year, and a little more, and the curse would have ended, but now that she has seen his face, he looks at the wax on his shirt, and the prince looks sad, so the youngest daughter does not know what to say.

s.t: "I did not want this," she said.
s.fr: « Je ne voulais pas cela, » dit-elle.

s.t: "Now I must go," the prince said.
s.fr: « Maintenant je dois partir, » dit le prince.

s.t: "Go where?" she asked.
s.fr: « Aller où ? » demanda-t-elle.

s.t: The prince did not speak.
s.fr: Le prince ne parla pas.

paras.summary: She says she is sorry, and the prince says he must go now; she asks where, but the prince does not speak.

s.t: The prince spoke.
s.fr: Le prince parla.

s.t: "I must go to the castle east of the sun and west of the moon."
s.fr: « Je dois aller au château à l’est du soleil et à l’ouest de la lune. »

s.t: "There, I must marry the troll princess," he said.
s.fr: « Là-bas, je dois épouser la princesse troll, » dit-il.

s.t: "I have seen her long nose," he said.
s.fr: « J’ai vu son long nez, » dit-il.

paras.summary: At last, the prince speaks, saying he must go to the castle east of the sun and west of the moon and marry the troll princess, who has a long nose.

s.t: The youngest daughter did not want him to go.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune ne voulait pas qu’il parte.

s.t: "Take me with you," she said.
s.fr: « Emmène-moi avec toi, » dit-elle.

s.t: "No one finds that castle," the prince said.
s.fr: « Personne ne trouve ce château, » dit le prince.

s.t: "I do not know the way either," he said.
s.fr: « Je ne connais pas le chemin non plus, » dit-il.

s.t: The youngest daughter was afraid for him.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune avait peur pour lui.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter does not want him to go and asks him to take her, but the prince says no one finds that castle, and he does not know the way either, so she is afraid for him.

s.t: Soon the castle shook.
s.fr: Bientôt le château trembla.

s.t: The prince and the castle both disappeared.
s.fr: Le prince et le château disparurent tous les deux.

s.t: The youngest daughter stood alone in a forest.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune se retrouva seule dans une forêt.

s.t: She decided to find the prince.
s.fr: Elle décida de trouver le prince.

paras.summary: Soon the ground begins to shake, and the prince and the castle both disappear, leaving the youngest daughter alone in a forest, where she decides to find him.

s.t: The youngest daughter walked through the forest for many days.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune marcha à travers la forêt pendant de nombreux jours.

s.t: Soon, she came to a small house.
s.fr: Bientôt, elle arriva à une petite maison.

s.t: An old woman sat by the house.
s.fr: Une vieille femme était assise près de la maison.

s.t: "I look for a prince, east of the sun and west of the moon."
s.fr: « Je cherche un prince, à l’est du soleil et à l’ouest de la lune. »

s.t: "I do not know that castle," the old woman said.
s.fr: « Je ne connais pas ce château, » dit la vieille femme.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter walks through the forest for many days until she comes to a small house, where an old woman sits, and when the youngest daughter says she is looking for a prince, east of the sun and west of the moon, the old woman says she does not know that castle, and is kind to the girl.

s.t: "But take this golden apple," she said.
s.fr: « Mais prends cette pomme d’or, » dit-elle.

s.t: "Take my horse, and ride to my sister," said the old woman.
s.fr: « Prends mon cheval, et va chez ma sœur, » dit la vieille femme.

s.t: "She may know the way."
s.fr: « Elle connaît peut-être le chemin. »

s.t: The youngest daughter thanked her and rode on.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune la remercia et continua sa route.

paras.summary: But she gives the youngest daughter a golden apple and her horse, telling her to ride to her sister, who may know the way, so the youngest daughter thanks her and rides on.

s.t: She came to the next old woman and asked the same question.
s.fr: Elle arriva chez la vieille femme suivante et lui posa la même question.

s.t: This old woman did not know the way either.
s.fr: Cette vieille femme ne connaissait pas non plus le chemin.

s.t: But she gave a golden comb, lent a horse, and sent her on her way.
s.fr: Mais elle donna un peigne doré, prêta un cheval, et la mit en route.

paras.summary: She comes to the next old woman and asks the same question; this old woman does not know the way either, but she gives a golden comb, lends a horse, and sends her on her way.

s.t: The youngest daughter thanked her and rode to a third old woman.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille la remercia et chevaucha vers une troisième vieille femme.

s.t: She asked the same question again.
s.fr: Elle posa la même question encore.

s.t: "But take this golden wheel," she said.
s.fr: « Mais prends cette roue dorée, » dit-elle.

s.t: "Now go and ask the four winds, for they may know the way."
s.fr: « Maintenant va et demande aux quatre vents, car ils peuvent connaître le chemin. »

paras.summary: The youngest daughter thanks her and rides to a third old woman, asking the same question again; this old woman does not know the way either, but she gives a golden wheel and tells her to ask the four winds, who may know the way.

s.t: The youngest daughter came to the East Wind.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille arriva au Vent de l’Est.

s.t: He was cold, and he blew against her face.
s.fr: Il était froid, et il souffla contre son visage.

s.t: "I look for a prince, east of the sun and west of the moon."
s.fr: « Je cherche un prince, à l’est du soleil et à l’ouest de la lune. »

s.t: "I have blown over many lands, but never so far," the East Wind said.
s.fr: « J’ai soufflé sur beaucoup de terres, mais jamais si loin, » dit le Vent de l’Est.

s.t: "My brother, the West Wind, is stronger, and he may know," he said.
s.fr: « Mon frère, le Vent de l’Ouest, est plus fort, et il peut savoir, » dit-il.

s.t: He lifted her into the sky and blew her over green hills.
s.fr: Il la souleva dans le ciel et la souffla par-dessus de vertes collines.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter comes to the East Wind, cold and blowing hard against her face, and asks for a prince, east of the sun and west of the moon; he has blown over many lands but never so far, and thinks his brother, the West Wind, may know, so he lifts her into the sky and blows her over green hills.

s.t: He set her down before his brother.
s.fr: Il la posa devant son frère.

s.t: The West Wind was larger, and his voice was loud.
s.fr: Le Vent de l’Ouest était plus grand, et sa voix était forte.

s.t: "I look for a prince, east of the sun and west of the moon."
s.fr: « Je cherche un prince, à l’est du soleil et à l’ouest de la lune. »

s.t: "I have never blown so far," said the West Wind.
s.fr: « Je n’ai jamais soufflé aussi loin, » dit le Vent de l’Ouest.

s.t: "But my brother, the South Wind, may know the way," he said.
s.fr: « Mais mon frère, le Vent du Sud, connaît peut-être le chemin, » dit-il.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter grows tired but does not stop, and the East Wind sets her down before the West Wind, who is larger and louder; she asks the same question, but he too has never blown so far and sends her on to his brother, the South Wind, lifting her over dark mountains.

s.t: He lifted her into the sky and blew her over dark mountains.
s.fr: Il la souleva dans le ciel et la souffla par-dessus de sombres montagnes.

s.t: The youngest daughter held on and did not look down.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille tint bon et ne regarda pas en bas.

s.t: The South Wind stood warm and strong beside the sea, which stretched far below.
s.fr: Le Vent du Sud se tenait chaud et fort près de la mer, qui s’étendait loin en bas.

s.t: "I look for a prince, east of the sun and west of the moon."
s.fr: « Je cherche un prince, à l’est du soleil et à l’ouest de la lune. »

s.t: "I have crossed wide seas, but never that far," he said.
s.fr: « J’ai traversé de larges mers, mais jamais aussi loin, » dit-il.

s.t: "Only my brother, the North Wind, may know the way," he said.
s.fr: « Seul mon frère, le Vent du Nord, connaît peut-être le chemin, » dit-il.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter holds on and does not look down, until she reaches the South Wind, warm and strong beside the sea; she asks again, and he has crossed wide seas but never that far, saying only his brother, the North Wind, may know the way.

s.t: The youngest daughter came to the North Wind.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune vint au Nord.

s.t: He was the oldest and strongest of the four winds.
s.fr: Il était le plus vieux et le plus fort des quatre vents.

s.t: "I look for a prince, east of the sun and west of the moon."
s.fr: « Je cherche un prince, à l’est du soleil et à l’ouest de la lune. »

s.t: "I went there once," the North Wind said.
s.fr: « J’y allai une fois, » dit le Vent du Nord.

s.t: "I blew an aspen leaf there once."
s.fr: « J’y soufflai une feuille de tremble une fois. »

s.t: "I was tired for days after," he said.
s.fr: « J’étais fatigué pendant des jours après, » dit-il.

s.t: "The way is far, over a wide sea," he said.
s.fr: « Le chemin est long, au-delà d’une mer large, » dit-il.

s.t: "I will try to blow you there," said the North Wind.
s.fr: « Je vais essayer de te souffler là-bas, » dit le Vent du Nord.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter comes to the North Wind, the oldest and strongest of the four, and asks for a prince, east of the sun and west of the moon; he went there once, blowing an aspen leaf there and staying tired for many days after, but though the way is far, over a wide sea, he agrees to try.

s.t: He lifted her into the sky and blew to the sea.
s.fr: Il la souleva dans le ciel et souffla vers la mer.

s.t: He blew all day and all night over the wide sea.
s.fr: Il souffla toute la journée et toute la nuit sur la grande mer.

s.t: "I am almost too tired to go on," said the North Wind.
s.fr: « Je suis presque trop fatigué pour continuer », dit le Vent du Nord.

s.t: But he blew on, over the last of the sea.
s.fr: Mais il souffla encore, au-dessus du dernier bout de mer.

paras.summary: He lifts her into the sky and blows to the sea, blowing all day and all night; he grows tired but does not stop, though his strength grows less and less, until he says he is almost too tired to go on.

s.t: At last, he saw land.
s.fr: Enfin, il aperçut la terre.

s.t: With his last strength, he set her down on the shore.
s.fr: Avec ses dernières forces, il la déposa sur le rivage.

s.t: A castle stood there.
s.fr: Un château se dressait là.

s.t: "This is the castle east of the sun and west of the moon," he said.
s.fr: « C’est le château à l’est du soleil et à l’ouest de la lune », dit-il.

paras.summary: But he blows on, over the last of the sea, until at last he sees land, and with his last strength he sets her down on the shore, where a castle stands: the castle east of the sun and west of the moon.

s.t: She came to the castle east of the sun and west of the moon.
s.fr: Elle arriva au château à l’est du soleil et à l’ouest de la lune.

s.t: There she saw the troll princess, with a long nose.
s.fr: Là, elle vit la princesse troll, avec un long nez.

s.t: "I will trade this golden apple for one night," the youngest daughter said.
s.fr: « Je vais échanger cette pomme dorée contre une nuit », dit la plus jeune fille.

s.t: The troll princess wanted gold, so she agreed.
s.fr: La princesse troll voulait de l’or, alors elle accepta.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter goes on and comes to the castle east of the sun and west of the moon, where she sees the troll princess, with a long nose, and trades a golden apple for one night there, which the troll princess agrees to for gold.

s.t: That night, the youngest daughter came to the prince's room.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, la plus jeune fille vint dans la chambre du prince.

s.t: He lay asleep, but he did not wake.
s.fr: Il était endormi, mais il ne se réveilla pas.

s.t: The trolls had given him a sleeping drink.
s.fr: Les trolls lui avaient donné une boisson soporifique.

s.t: The youngest daughter cried to him.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille pleura vers lui.

s.t: Soon she had to leave the room.
s.fr: Bientôt elle dut quitter la chambre.

paras.summary: That night, the youngest daughter comes to the prince's room, but he lies asleep and does not wake, for the trolls have given him a sleeping drink; she cries to him all night, but soon she must leave.

s.t: She traded the golden comb for one more night there.
s.fr: Elle échangea le peigne doré contre une nuit de plus là-bas.

s.t: Again, the prince lay asleep and did not wake.
s.fr: De nouveau, le prince était endormi et ne se réveilla pas.

s.t: The youngest daughter cried beside him all night.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille pleura à côté de lui toute la nuit.

s.t: Captives lived in the castle, and they heard her every night.
s.fr: Des captifs vivaient dans le château, et ils l’entendaient chaque nuit.

s.t: By day, the captives saw the prince, for he had no drink.
s.fr: Le jour, les captifs voyaient le prince, car il n’avait pas de boisson.

s.t: They decided to tell him what they had heard.
s.fr: Ils décidèrent de lui dire ce qu’ils avaient entendu.

paras.summary: She trades the golden comb for one more night, and again the prince lies asleep with the sleeping drink in him, so the youngest daughter cries beside him all night; captives in the castle hear her every night, and since they see the prince undrugged by day, they decide to tell him what they have heard.

s.t: The captives told the prince what they knew.
s.fr: Les captifs dirent au prince ce qu’ils savaient.

s.t: "Someone cried by your bed every night," they said.
s.fr: « Quelqu’un a pleuré près de ton lit chaque nuit, » dirent-ils.

s.t: The prince did not know who cried.
s.fr: Le prince ne savait pas qui avait pleuré.

s.t: But he thought it might be her.
s.fr: Mais il pensa que c’était peut-être elle.

paras.summary: The captives tell the prince what they know, someone crying by his bed every night, and though he does not know who cried, he thinks of this all day and believes it might be her.

s.t: That night, the trolls gave him the sleeping drink.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, les trolls lui donnèrent la boisson soporifique.

s.t: The prince did not drink it.
s.fr: Le prince ne la but pas.

s.t: No one saw him pour it away.
s.fr: Personne ne le vit la verser.

s.t: He waited in the dark for her to come.
s.fr: Il attendit dans l’obscurité qu’elle vienne.

paras.summary: That night, the trolls give him the sleeping drink, but the prince does not drink it, and no one sees him pour it away as he waits in the dark for her to come.

s.t: The youngest daughter traded the golden wheel for one more night.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune échangea la roue dorée contre une nuit de plus.

s.t: She came to his room in the dark.
s.fr: Elle vint dans sa chambre dans l’obscurité.

s.t: The prince was awake.
s.fr: Le prince était éveillé.

s.t: "Is it you?" he asked.
s.fr: « Est-ce vous ? » dit-il.

paras.summary: The youngest daughter trades the golden wheel for one more night and comes to his room in the dark, and this time the prince is awake and asks if it is her.

s.t: "Yes, it is," she said.
s.fr: « Oui, c’est moi », dit-elle.

s.t: The prince was glad, and he held her, for it was her.
s.fr: Le prince était content, et il la tint dans ses bras, car c’était elle.

paras.summary: She says yes, and he knows it is her; the prince is glad and holds her, and she holds him too, glad it is him, for he had waited so long for this night, and so had she.

s.t: The prince told her they must go away from this castle.
s.fr: Le prince lui dit qu’ils devaient quitter ce château.

s.t: "The trolls will not let me go," he said.
s.fr: « Les trolls ne me laisseront pas partir », dit-il.

s.t: "I will make one test," said the prince.
s.fr: « Je vais faire une épreuve », dit le prince.

s.t: He showed her his shirt, with the wax still on it.
s.fr: Il lui montra sa chemise, avec la cire encore dessus.

paras.summary: The prince tells her they must go away from this castle, for the trolls will not let him go, so he will make one test, showing her his shirt, with the wax still on it.

s.t: "I will marry only the one who can wash this white," he said.
s.fr: « Je n’épouserai que celle qui pourra laver cela en blanc », dit-il.

s.t: "The troll princess will try first," he said.
s.fr: « La princesse des trolls essaiera en premier », dit-il.

s.t: "But she will fail," said the prince.
s.fr: « Mais elle échouera, » dit le prince.

s.t: "Then you will try," he said.
s.fr: « Alors vous essaierez, » dit-il.

s.t: The youngest daughter agreed.
s.fr: La plus jeune fille accepta.

paras.summary: He says he will marry only the one who can wash it white, and though the troll princess will try first and fail, then she will try, and the youngest daughter agrees to the plan.

s.t: Soon, morning came to the castle.
s.fr: Bientôt, le matin arriva au château.

s.t: The prince called the troll princess and her mother to him.
s.fr: Le prince appela la princesse troll et sa mère auprès de lui.

s.t: The troll princess wanted to be his bride.
s.fr: La princesse troll voulait être sa épouse.

s.t: She believed she could wash it.
s.fr: Elle croyait qu’elle pouvait le laver.

paras.summary: Soon, morning comes to the castle, and the prince calls the troll princess and her mother to him, saying again that he will marry only the one who can wash his shirt white; the troll princess wants to be his bride and believes she could wash it.

s.t: The troll princess tried to wash the shirt.
s.fr: La princesse troll essaya de laver la chemise.

s.t: The more she washed it, the darker it grew.
s.fr: Plus elle la lavait, plus elle devenait sombre.

s.t: Her mother tried next, but the shirt grew darker still.
s.fr: Sa mère essaya ensuite, mais la chemise devint encore plus sombre.

paras.summary: The troll princess tries to wash the shirt, but the more she washes it, the darker it grows, and her mother tries next, but the shirt grows darker still, for the trolls cannot wash it white.

s.t: Soon the youngest daughter stepped forward.
s.fr: Bientôt la fille la plus jeune s’avança.

s.t: "Let me try," she said.
s.fr: « Laissez-moi essayer, » dit-elle.

s.t: The troll princess laughed at her.
s.fr: La princesse troll se moqua d’elle.

s.t: But the prince let her try.
s.fr: Mais le prince la laissa essayer.

s.t: The youngest daughter washed the shirt.
s.fr: La fille la plus jeune lava la chemise.

s.t: Soon it was white.
s.fr: Bientôt elle était blanche.

paras.summary: Soon the youngest daughter steps forward and asks to try, and though the troll princess laughs at her, the prince lets her try, and she washes the shirt until soon it is white.

s.t: "You will be my true bride," the prince said.
s.fr: « Tu seras ma vraie épouse, » dit le prince.

s.t: The troll princess and her mother grew angry.
s.fr: La princesse troll et sa mère devinrent furieuses.

s.t: They ran away into the mountains and never came back.
s.fr: Elles s’enfuirent dans les montagnes et ne revinrent jamais.

s.t: The prince freed all the captives in the castle.
s.fr: Le prince libéra tous les captifs du château.

paras.summary: The prince tells her she will be his true bride, and the troll princess and her mother grow angry and run away into the mountains and never come back, so the prince frees all the captives in the castle.

s.t: The prince married the youngest daughter.
s.fr: Le prince épousa la fille la plus jeune.

s.t: They left the castle and went far away together.
s.fr: Ils quittèrent le château et partirent loin ensemble.

s.t: Her family was glad to see her again.
s.fr: Sa famille fut heureuse de la revoir.

s.t: They never saw the trolls again.
s.fr: Ils ne revirent jamais les trolls.

paras.summary: The prince marries the youngest daughter, and they leave the castle and go far away together; her family is glad to see her again, and they never see the trolls again.
